cost.notes: International estimated expenses, 9 months fall/spring (2026-27): tuition and fees combined $20,100, housing and meals $12,700, books $1,200, medical insurance $2,300 (shown as other costs) = $36,300 before scholarships; $30,800 after the Global Select scholarship. Kansas rates are announced in July, so actual cost may differ. One-time $200 international enrollment fee and $150 orientation fee

test_policy.notes: Option 1 admits international freshmen on high school grades and the SAT or ACT is not required. Option 2 admits on test results alone (SAT 1060 combined EBRW+Math with 490+ on each section, or ACT composite 21 with 18+ on every section) and is meant for students who want admission before finishing high school or attended an unrecognized school. SAT/ACT are not used for the Global Select scholarship.

requirements.notes: Application fee depends on processing speed: Basic $75 (4-5 weeks), Standard $150 (2-3 weeks), Premium $250 (3 business days); fees are non-refundable. Required: certification of financial support, bank statement, official transcripts from all schools (front and back), passport name page, and TOEFL/IELTS/SAT/ACT results are optional at application (see English notes). The grade needed for admission under Option 1 depends on the country; the specific minimum was not on the pages read. Select 'International Undergraduate or Intensive English' when starting the application.

english_policy.waiver_notes: A TOEFL or IELTS score is not required to apply; it can be sent later, or WSU tests English after arrival (WSU English Proficiency Exam, $75). Students who do not meet the English requirement get conditional admission and enroll in the Intensive English Language Center; the I-20 then lists Intensive English with a note of the academic admission. Half-time academic study alongside Intensive English is allowed with lower scores (TOEFL 61-71 / 3.5 new scale, IELTS 5.5, Duolingo 95-104, PTE 40-48). Also accepted: SAT EBRW 410, ACT English 20, Cambridge A/AS English grade C, 24 U.S. college credits, four years of U.S. high school English with C+. Tests must be less than two years old; IELTS General Training and One Skill Retake are not accepted.

aid.notes: Global Select Scholarship: automatic at admission with one scholarship question on the application; undergraduates need a 3.0 GPA (or international equivalent); a 36% tuition discount (tuition only, not fees) worth an estimated $5,500 per academic year at 12 credit hours, renewable to the end of the program; SAT/ACT not used. Continuing-student scholarships (usually $500-$2,500 per year) require a year at WSU first, and there are no scholarships based on financial need.
